t: A ten-cent RISC-V chip with a 2.4 GHz radio and a USB port.
steps: Order a MuseLab nanoCH57x board from Tindie for about $3.50. It currently ships with the CH572D chip.
Install a RISC-V GCC compiler on your computer.
Download the free ch32fun toolkit from GitHub.
Open the blink demo in the ch32fun CH5xx examples folder.
Hold the BOOT button and plug the board into USB-C. The board starts its USB bootloader.
Build the demo and upload it over USB. Watch the user LED blink.
Try the BLE beacon demo next. Then try the low-power demo.
